This permanently deletes your account and everything backed up in the cloud: results, favorites, streaks, your username and your friends. The progress on this device is deleted too. This can't be undone.
Couldn't delete the account. Check your connection and try again
Sends anonymous usage counts (like which screens are opened) and crash reports. They contain no account, device or personal data.
The daily streak counts every finished daily puzzle, in any language.
Turn over two cards and find the pairs
No one has finished today's puzzle yet.
The table isn't available right now.
Sign in to join the tables.
At least one game stays on.
Tap a tube, then the tube to pour into
Start again from the beginning, moves are kept
Tap to open, long-press to flag. Double-tap a number to open around it
Flag mode is on: tapping flags a cell. Tap to turn it off
Flag mode is off: tapping opens a cell. Tap to turn it on
Row %1$d, column %2$d, open, no mines around
Row %1$d, column %2$d, the mine you opened
Find the hidden 5-letter word in 6 tries. Type a real word and press ENTER.
After each try the letters change color: green is in the right place, yellow is in the word but in another place, gray is not in the word.
Solve it to grow your streak. Running out of tries resets it.
Your streak only breaks when you lose a puzzle. You pick the word language when you build your feed.
Turn over two cards per move and find the 6 pairs.
Two cards with the same shape stay open. Different shapes are a mistake, and they turn back after a moment.
A mistake only counts: you can always go on. Finding every pair wins the game.
Fewer moves and a faster time are better. The shapes are told apart by their form, not only their color.
Sort the colors until every tube holds one color only (or is empty).
Tap a tube to lift it, then tap another tube to pour into it. The top color goes onto an empty tube, or onto the same color, as much as fits.
There is no losing. If you get stuck, undo the last pour or restart the board. Your moves keep counting.
Every color also has its own shape, so you can tell them apart without the colors.
Open every cell that has no mine. Opening a mine loses the game.
A number tells how many mines touch that cell, diagonals too.
Tap to open a cell. Long-press to flag a cell you think is a mine, or turn on the flag button to flag with a tap.
Double-tap a number whose flags match it to open all the other cells around it at once. A wrong flag makes that lose.
Your first tap is always safe, and every board can be solved by logic alone, so you never have to guess.
Notes mode is on: numbers are written as small notes. Tap to turn it off
Notes mode is off: numbers are placed in the cell. Tap to turn it on
Fill the 9x9 board so every row, every column and every 3x3 box holds the numbers 1 to 9 once.
Tap an empty cell, then a number below. The cells that are already filled can not be changed.
A wrong number counts as a mistake and shows in red, but you can keep going and erase it. A correct number is final.
Turn on the pencil to write small notes of the numbers a cell could be. The eraser takes back a wrong number or clears the notes.
Every board can be solved by logic alone, so you never have to guess.
Tap a light: it and its neighbors switch. Put them all out
This board can be solved in %1$d moves or fewer
Start again from the beginning, moves are kept
Put out every light on the board.
Tapping a light switches it and the lights right above, below, left and right of it: the ones that were on go out, the ones that were off come on.
There is no losing. If you get lost, start again from the beginning. Your moves keep counting. Tapping the same light twice cancels out.
Every board can be solved. The number next to the moves tells in how many taps at most.
Tap a tile in line with the empty space to slide it. Put the numbers in order
Start again from the beginning, moves are kept
Tile %1$d, row %2$d, column %3$d, in its place
Slide the tiles until the numbers are in order, 1 at the top left, the empty space last.
Tap a tile in the same row or column as the empty space: it slides into the space, and the tiles between them move along with it. That is one move.
There is no losing. If you get lost, start again from the beginning. Your moves keep counting.
Every board can be solved. A tile turns green when it is in its place.
Pick a number, an operation, then another number
The target can be reached in %1$d moves at the fewest
Take back the last operation, moves are kept
Start again from the beginning, moves are kept
Reach the target number using the four numbers you are given. You do not have to use all of them.
Tap a number, then an operation (+, −, ×, ÷), then another number. The two numbers are replaced by the result, and the result can be used again.
Every number can be used only once. Results must be whole numbers above zero: a subtraction can not reach zero or go below, and a division must come out even. Numbers that do not fit are dimmed.
There is no losing. If you get stuck, take back the last operation or start again. Your moves keep counting. The faster the better.
Every target can be reached. The number next to the moves is the fewest operations it takes.
Tap a tile to turn it. Connect every pipe, no open ends
This board can be solved in %1$d taps at the fewest
Start again from the beginning, moves are kept
Connect all the pipes so that no pipe has an open end. An open end is a pipe side that does not meet a pipe of its neighbor.
Tap a tile to turn it a quarter clockwise. Sides that meet turn green, open ends are gray with a ring.
There is no losing. If you get lost, start again from the beginning. Your moves keep counting.
Every board can be solved. The number next to the moves is the fewest taps it takes.
Everyone solves the same puzzle today.
Pick the games you want to play.
Pick both to get puzzles in either language.
The language of the menus and texts. The daily puzzle uses it too.
Finish today's puzzle every day to keep it going. Winning or losing doesn't matter, finishing does.
If you miss a day, it starts again from zero.
Every 7 days in a row earns a streak freeze. It covers a missed day by itself. You can keep one at a time.
The number of puzzles you solved in this feed without the guide, in any game.
Losing a puzzle or leaving one unfinished doesn't change it.
A puzzle you solve with the guide doesn't count.
Sign in to back up your progress
Done for today. A new puzzle comes tomorrow!
Everyone solves the same board today.
Open a cell in the middle to start. The first open is always safe.
The numbers around this cell prove it holds no mine. Open it.
The numbers around this cell prove it holds a mine. Flag it.
No move is certain right now. Check that your flags are right.
This digit is wrong. Erase it first.
Only %1$d fits in this cell: its row, column and box already have all the others.
%1$d can only go in this cell of its row, column or box.
Tap this pipe %1$d time(s): that is the way that needs the fewest taps.
Tap this light. It is part of the shortest way to put them all out.
Slide this tile into the empty cell. It is the first step of the shortest way home.
Tap the ringed tube, then the next ringed tube to pour into it.
No pour finishes the tubes from here. Undo a few pours or start again.
Take %1$d %3$s %2$d: it is the first step of the shortest way.
This card matches the one that is face up.
From these numbers the target cannot be reached any more. Start the puzzle over and ask again.
The guide has nothing to add here.
The puzzle you left half done will be forgotten. Your results stay.
Draw one line from number 1 to the last number. It has to pass every square exactly once.
Drag your finger from square to square, or tap a square next to the end of the line. The numbers must be passed in order.
The last number is the last square of the line, so fill everything else first. Drag back over the line to shorten it.
Your mistakes (squares you took back) and your moves are counted. The hint button shows the next squares, but a board you needed a hint for is left out of your statistics.
Drag from number 1 to the last number and fill every square
The last number comes last. Fill every other square first
The line leads nowhere from here. Take a square back
One Line board, %1$d of %2$d squares filled, next number %3$d
Row %1$d, column %2$d, end of the line
Clear the line and start again
Every daily crossword starts with 3 stars. You lose them as you make mistakes.
Every wrong letter you type counts as a mistake, even if you take it back.
Stars decide your place on the daily table, then the time.
Tap a tower, then the tower the top disk goes to. Move every disk to the goal tower
This puzzle can be solved in %1$d moves at the fewest
Start again from the beginning, moves are kept
How to play: Tower of Hanoi
Move all the disks onto the goal tower, the one marked Goal.
Tap a tower to pick up its top disk, then tap the tower it goes to. Only one disk moves at a time.
A disk can only go onto an empty tower or onto a bigger disk, never onto a smaller one.
There is no losing. Start again if you get lost, your moves keep counting. The number next to the moves is the fewest it takes.
Move the top disk of tower %1$s onto tower %2$s. It is the first step of the shortest way.
Place a queen in every row and every column. No two queens may share a row, a column or a diagonal. Tap again to take one away
This puzzle can be solved in %1$d moves at the fewest
Take away the queens you placed, moves are kept
Row %1$d, column %2$d, queen attacked by another queen
Put a queen in every row and every column of the board.
No two queens may be in the same row, the same column or on the same diagonal. Queens that attack each other turn red.
Some queens are locked from the start (with a lock mark). You cannot move them, build around them.
Tap an empty cell to place a queen, tap it again to take it away. There is no losing. Start again if you get lost, your moves keep counting. The number next to the moves is the fewest it takes.
Put a queen in row %1$d, column %2$d. It is part of a way to finish the board.
Take away the queen in row %1$d, column %2$d. It cannot be part of a finished board.
Put a tent next to every tree. No two tents touch, not even at a corner. The numbers count the tents in each row and column. Tap twice for grass
Clear the board and start again
Row %1$d, column %2$d, grass, no tent here
Row %1$d, column %2$d, tent that breaks a rule
Put a tent next to every tree, above, below or beside it. Every tent belongs to one tree.
No two tents may touch, not even at a corner.
The numbers beside the rows and above the columns say how many tents each one holds. A tent that breaks a rule turns red.
Tap a cell once for a tent, again for grass (your note that there is no tent), a third time to clear it. The grass is only for you. There is only one right answer, and you can always work it out.
Put a tent in row %1$d, column %2$d. The trees and the numbers leave no other place for it.
Take away the tent in row %1$d, column %2$d. It cannot be part of the finished board.
Fill the 9x9 board so every row, every column and every region (the shapes with thick lines around them) holds the numbers 1 to 9 once.
The regions are not squares: each is a shape of nine cells with a thick border around it. Look at the shapes, not only at the rows and columns.
Tap an empty cell, then a number below. The cells that are already filled can not be changed.
A wrong number counts as a mistake and shows in red, but you can keep going and erase it. A correct number is final. Turn on the pencil to write small notes.
Every board can be solved by logic alone, so you never have to guess.
Only %1$d fits in this cell: its row, column and region already have all the others.
%1$d can only go in this cell of its row, column or region.
Slide the blocks to clear a way for the orange block to the exit on the right. Drag a block, or tap it and then tap where it should go
This puzzle can be solved in %1$d moves at the fewest
Put the blocks back as they were, moves are kept
The orange block, %1$d cells long, row %2$d, column %3$d. Drive it to the exit on the right
Exit, on the right of the middle row
Get the orange block out through the exit on the right side of the middle row.
Blocks slide only the way they lie, along their length, and cannot go over each other. Drag a block, or tap it and then tap the cell it should go to.
Sliding a block by one cell or by several in one go is one move. There is no losing: you can always start again, and your moves keep counting.
The number next to the moves is the fewest it takes. It is not easy to reach, so try to get close.
Slide the marked block up by %1$d. It is the first step of the shortest way.
Slide the marked block down by %1$d. It is the first step of the shortest way.
Slide the marked block left by %1$d. It is the first step of the shortest way.
Slide the marked block right by %1$d. It is the first step of the shortest way.
Copied. Paste it in a chat
Double-tap the board to zoom in
Zoom out to the whole board
Clue for the answer going across, %1$d letters: %2$s
Clue for the answer going down, %1$d letters: %2$s

The board is big, so it starts as a far view. Double-tap a spot to zoom in on it. The dark squares hold clues, and the arrow on the edge of a square shows where the answer starts and which way it runs.

When zoomed in, drag the board with a finger to look around. Tap a square, then type with the keyboard. Tap the same square again to switch between the answer going across and the one going down. Double-tap again, or press the corner button, to zoom out.
A wrong letter counts as a mistake and shows in red, but you can keep going and take it back. A right letter is final. In the daily crossword, fewer mistakes earn more stars.
The key at the bottom right moves to the next answer. Letters where two answers cross have to fit both.
The letter in row %1$d, column %2$d is wrong. Take it back first.
The letter %1$s belongs in row %2$d, column %3$d.
